failures.title: CI failed on first push: conflicting pnpm versions
failures.whatHappened: The CI workflow pinned `pnpm/action-setup@v4` to version 10 while package.json's `packageManager` field pinned pnpm@10.32.1. pnpm's own version check treats those as two different sources of truth and refuses to run.
failures.howCaught: First GitHub Actions run on main failed immediately in the 'Run pnpm/action-setup@v4' step, before lint/typecheck/build even started.
failures.fix: Dropped the explicit `version: 10` from the workflow step so action-setup reads the version from package.json's packageManager field instead.
failures.lesson: When package.json already pins a packageManager version, don't also pin it in CI config — pick one source of truth.

failures.title: CI typecheck failed: Next.js's generated route types weren't there yet
failures.whatHappened: `app/layout.tsx` uses Next.js's typed-routes `LayoutProps<'/'>` global, which only exists once Next.js has generated `.next/types` (gitignored). CI ran a standalone `tsc --noEmit` before anything had generated those types, so it failed on `Cannot find name 'LayoutProps'` even though `pnpm build` passed fine locally (build generates the types itself first).
failures.howCaught: Second CI run still failed, now in the typecheck step specifically, right after fixing the pnpm version issue.
failures.fix: Added a `next typegen` step before `pnpm typecheck` in CI, which generates just the route types without a full build.
failures.lesson: A typed-routes feature means `tsc --noEmit` alone isn't a complete typecheck in CI — it depends on a generation step that `next build`/`next dev` normally does implicitly.

failures.title: PROMPT_CONFLICT checker misread its own award-amount match as the fund total
failures.whatHappened: The PROMPT_CONFLICT rule's regex extraction scans every "$X" mention for nearby words like "fund" or "total" to guess the stated funding total. It didn't exclude mentions already claimed by the award-amount regexes ("up to $X", a "$X-$Y" range), so a prompt like "A fund for nonprofits. Awards up to $25,000" misread the award figure as the fund total too, because the word "fund" fell inside that mention's context window.
failures.howCaught: Unit test for PROMPT_CONFLICT (tests/unit/promptConflict.test.ts): a case asserting the award-max mismatch message contained both the expected and actual numbers failed because the extractor also fired a false fundingTotal mismatch, producing the wrong message at index 0.
failures.fix: Tracked the index ranges already claimed by award-amount matches and skip any money mention inside those ranges when scanning for a fund total.
failures.lesson: A regex-based extractor needs to track which spans of text it's already consumed, or a second heuristic pass will double-count the same number under a different label.

Human review of generated rubrics for fairness and plain language before customer use
An eval set built from real (anonymized) customer programs, run in CI on every prompt or model change, with a release gate
Tracking edit distance: how much admins change each AI section, as the main quality signal
